newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end down, hit by currency qualms.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end down, hit by currency qualms.

text.p: Singapore shares ended weaker on Monday as caution about regional currency stability overtook an otherwise optimistic view of the country's electronics companies, dealers said.
"Electronics look good for the second half, but the currency question is keeping people out," said one dealer.
"Investors desperately want things to be better, but the signs are still not all there," said another dealer.
Singapore's blue chip Straits Times Industrials Index reflected the cautious approach of the international fund managers, slipping 5.95 points to 1,975.01 at the close.
The Stock Exchange of Singapore's electronics index showed the day's only meagre sign of optimism, hitting an intraday high of 162.89 before slipping back to 157.92, a rise of just 0.23 points.
Many market eyes were on Creative Technology and Venture Manufacturing, rivals in the multimedia business in which Venture launched a new product last week.
Early trade saw Venture stock climb to a high of Singapore $8.00, although it ended the day at S$6.90, up just five cents.
Creative came under renewed pressure ahead of results due in the U.S. later in the day and ended down S$0.60 at S$33.90.
Monday's biggest faller, however, was City Developments, down S$0.80 at S$13.10.
Small cap stocks joined electronics as the day's most active counters in a trading session which saw a healthy 215.8 million shares traded to give 244 fallers and 138 gainers.
